PullRequest.Title: Speed up component fixture execution
PullRequest.Body:
Speed up the full Component Fixtures workload without skipping checks, fixtures, or leak detection.

- Capture allocation and timer-scheduling errors immediately, but defer expensive stack formatting and source-map expansion until diagnostics need the stack.
- Initialize source maps once, before asynchronous fixture-render timeouts start, so cold-cache error fixtures still render successfully.
- Distribute independent Playwright tests within files across the existing worker pool.
- Add regression tests for lazy stack formatting, leak reporting, and preservation of original allocation/scheduling locations.

## Motivation and measurements

The Component Fixtures job on #335932 took 20m17s, including 13m05s capturing screenshots and 5m44s running interaction tests. Profiling identified eager source-mapped diagnostic stack formatting as a major rendering cost.

Local before/after measurements used the same Windows checkout, Chromium version, complete fixture list, two Playwright workers, and an already-running fixture server:

| Workload | Before | After | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| All 1,765 fixture screenshots | 589.74s | 332.82s | 43.6% |
| All 15 interaction tests | 82.79s | 76.42s | 7.7% |
| Combined | 672.53s | 409.24s | 39.1% |

Scenarios.Scenario: Headless rendering and screenshot capture of the full component-fixture catalog
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each fixture initializes its browser-side fixture host, installs leak tracking and virtual time, performs async render/layout, then becomes available for screenshot capture. The changed one-time Error.stack warm-up is on the first headless render's critical path; allocation and timer stack formatting is now off the successful critical path and occurs only for diagnostics.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: source-map-support synchronously fetches generated-script source maps via XMLHttpRequest when Error.stack is formatted
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Cold cache: source maps needed by the first formatted stack are fetched once per browser/module context and cached by source-map-support; warm successful fixtures perform no per-disposable stack access after this diff. On a leak, only reported root stacks are formatted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same source-map boundary was reached eagerly by every DisposableTracker allocation and every virtual timer/rAF stack capture; the diff reduces this to one initialization plus diagnostic-only accesses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The explicit first warm-up blocks initial headless fixture setup, but prevents cold source-map initialization from racing asynchronous timeout diagnostics. The prior path formatted stacks during every tracked allocation, repeatedly consuming CPU on render and potentially triggering cold synchronous map reads.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The workload contains roughly 1,765 screenshots; within each render cost formerly scaled with the number of disposable allocations and scheduled timers, while the changed successful path scales only with Error capture and bounded virtual events.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A fixture owns one VirtualTimeProcessor whose events are executed serially with explicit 200-event render and 1,000-event teardown caps. The screenshot command's outer concurrency is unchanged by this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: source-map-support caches fetched maps within the browser context. The new sourceMapsInitialized flag coalesces explicit warm-up to one access per loaded fixture module; lazy Error objects retain unsymbolized capture data until a leak/trace is rendered.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call flow from global DisposableTracker and virtual timer wrappers to Error.stack was replaced with retained Error objects and lazy getters; source-map retrieval is explicitly synchronous.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact source-map cache reuse depends on browser-page reuse, but the before/after workload measurement and per-allocation mechanism strongly establish the removed cost.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff removes repeated diagnostic formatting from the successful render path while preserving bounded failure diagnostics; the single warm-up is lower-cardinality than the work it replaces.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each test performs one page.goto to the local component-explorer server, waits for a fixture selector, then executes DOM interactions/assertions. fullyParallel changes assignment of independent tests to workers but does not add work to an individual test's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Navigate a fresh browser page to the local component-explorer HTTP server and load fixture assets
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One navigation per test before and after the diff; tests are not coalesced, and effective simultaneous requests remain bounded by Playwright workers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same one-navigation-per-test workload ran across the worker pool, but tests within a file were serialized, leaving workers idle near the tail of uneven files.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Navigation and fixture loading remain on each test's critical path. Scheduling can overlap requests from tests in the same file, but only within the pre-existing worker cap.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Runtime scales with the number and duration distribution of interaction tests; parallelism is bounded by the worker count rather than test count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Playwright's existing worker-pool limit remains authoritative. fullyParallel lets tests from the same file occupy otherwise-idle workers; it does not create concurrency beyond the configured/default worker count and there is no unbounded Promise fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Workers/browser contexts may reuse the local server's built assets and OS/browser caches; no cache key, invalidation, or cold/warm behavior changes in the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: Playwright config changes only fullyParallel, while each test still opens exactly one local fixture URL.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runner hardware determines the default worker count and exact speedup; this does not change the bounded-concurrency conclusion.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The change improves tail utilization without increasing maximum worker concurrency or boundary-call cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: ToolsTabNarrow and PromptMigration fixture rendering with deferred paint
Scenarios.CriticalPath: For these two headless fixture variants, opacity is set to zero immediately before the existing async render/virtual-time work and restored immediately after it; screenshot capture occurs after render completion. Layout and fixture construction still run on the same critical path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly two fixture definitions, each rendered for its configured theme variants; the added work is two style assignments per render.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each render remains serial inside its fixture's virtual-time processor; only two named fixture definitions opt in. No new concurrent tasks are created.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme and syntax-highlighting setup retain existing caches; deferPaint adds no cache. The fixtures use mocked in-memory file services rather than real filesystem/network calls.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the option is gated to headless mode and wraps only the existing render await.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Browser compositor savings vary by fixture complexity, but no scaling regression is introduced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The bounded opacity writes avoid intermediate presentation and do not add layout reads, I/O, or retained state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Voice-mode onboarding waveform start, suspension, resize, and theme redraw
Scenarios.CriticalPath: While active, requestAnimationFrame invokes draw once per frame. Start now clears the prior timestamp, and non-running resize/theme redraws use zero elapsed time before the same canvas clear/fill operation.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost remains one canvas draw per active frame plus isolated resize/theme/reduced-motion redraws.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A MutableDisposable keeps at most one scheduled animation frame; stop cancels it. No changed concurrency or queue growth exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; stroke style and geometry behavior are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guards only alter elapsed-time calculation and do not add frame scheduling or drawing operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual frame rate and canvas size vary, but operation count is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Leak and virtual-scheduler diagnostic reporting in unit tests and failed fixtures
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Successful tracking/scheduling captures Error objects without formatting. If leak or execution-history diagnostics are requested, stack getters format the original allocation/scheduling sites on that diagnostic path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronous source-map lookup when a lazily captured browser Error stack is first consumed
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Only uncovered/reportable leak roots (at most 10 in formatted leak output) or events included in explicitly requested histories consume stack getters; successful runs do not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Stacks were formatted at every allocation/schedule regardless of whether any diagnostic was emitted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the successful rendering/test path; on a failure/reporting path it preserves the pre-diff diagnostic cost.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Capture allocations scale with tracked disposables and scheduled events as before; expensive formatting now scales with reported leaks or explicitly rendered history rather than all successful allocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: VirtualClock executes events serially and histories are bounded by processor max-event limits in fixture runs. Real-time recording appends once per fired timer while its caller owns the history array.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: V8 memoizes a formatted Error.stack and source-map-support caches maps; the same Error is shared by event source and trace so subsequent diagnostic reads reuse the captured stack.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: lazy getters and diagnostic consumers are explicit in the changed and surrounding code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Error-object retention size versus preformatted strings is runtime-dependent, but lifetimes are bounded by tracker/event/history ownership and strings with mapped stacks were previously retained instead.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR converts eager diagnostic work to demand-driven work without unbounded retention or a new boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files and all diff pages. No diff-introduced performance regression met the reporting threshold. The principal change is a well-evidenced fix for repeated eager source-mapped stack formatting; the attempted internal regression-fix record could not be persisted because the reporting tool failed twice.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
